producer_report.summary: The negative end-to-end test now builds its record from an event whose total_cost_usd (0.75) really differs from the per-model costUSD sum (0.30). It goes through the same parse and record helper as the positive test, and no record is edited by hand. Before calling check_invocation it asserts that the reported total differs from the modelUsage sum, then asserts exactly one Reconciliation violation naming "per-model costs sum". Doc comments on the test and the fixture say token disagreement cannot arise through the parser under the modelUsage definition. CHANGELOG.md records the definition and says the test covers only the cost disagreement. I disabled the cost comparison in reconcile.rs and the negative test failed (0 violations instead of 1); I then restored the check, so the final diff leaves it intact. The full test run, clippy and fmt all pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a_result_whose_totals_disagree_with_model_usage_is_flagged_end_to_end passes. It builds the record from a result event with modelUsage for the requested model and a total_cost_usd that differs from the per-model costUSD sum. It uses the same parse and record-building helper as the positive test. It asserts, before calling check_invocation, that the record's reported total differs from the modelUsage sum. It then asserts exactly one Reconciliation violation whose detail names the per-model cost sum.
criteria_check.evidence: invocation.rs: test uses record_from(DISAGREEING) (total_cost_usd 0.75 vs costUSD 0.10+0.20), asserts models_used contains MODEL and |reported-per_model|>0.01, then asserts found.len()==1 and detail contains "per-model costs sum". Passes in cargo test; fails when the cost check in reconcile.rs is disabled (shown, then restored).
